p2Appendix.title: isFinalizing latch is never reset - a recording started during finalization cannot be stopped and is silently killed and stranded
p2Appendix.evidence: `private var isFinalizing = false` (line 82) is set true in stopAndSave() (line 179) and never reset anywhere in the file. stopAndSave() sets `isRecording = false` (line 193) then launches `serviceScope.launch { saveRecording(tempFile) }` (line 204). While that save copies the (potentially large) MP4, onStartCommand's only re-entry guard is `if (isRecording) return START_NOT_STICKY` (line 99), so a second consent flow starts a full new projection+recorder session. During this window the notification Stop action is dead: `private fun stopAndSave() { if (isFinalizing) return ... }` (lines 177-179). saveRecording()'s finally then executes `pendingTempFile = null` (line 223), discarding the reference to the SECOND session's file, and finishService() calls `stopSelf()` (lines 328-331) -> onDestroy stops the second recorder via `runCatching { mediaRecorder?.stop() }` and releases resources (lines 104-116), but `pendingTempFile?.delete()` is a no-op on null - the second recording is silently terminated mid-capture and its .mp4 stays stranded in the Movies temp dir, never saved and never cleaned.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Reset isFinalizing (and reject new starts) around the finalize window: either set isFinalizing=false when the save completes and guard startRecording() with it, or key stopAndSave() re-entrancy per session instead of a one-way latch.

p2Appendix.title: MediaController built asynchronously can land after onStopListening; next listen cycle overwrites it without release, leaking the controller and its Player.Listener
p2Appendix.evidence: connectToSession() resolves the controller asynchronously: `val future = MediaController.Builder(this, token).buildAsync(); future.addListener({ ... mediaController = future.get(); mediaController?.addListener(tilePlayerListener) ... }, MoreExecutors.directExecutor())` (lines 75-86). onStopListening() calls releaseController() (lines 38-41), but if the QS panel is closed before the future completes, releaseController() sees `mediaController == null` and does nothing; the callback then assigns the connected controller and attaches tilePlayerListener AFTER the tile stopped listening. On the next panel open, onStartListening() -> connectToSession() runs again and the callback overwrites `mediaController = future.get()` (line 78) - the previous connected instance is never removeListener'd nor release()'d. Each iteration of this open/close race leaks one MediaController binder connection to AudioPlaybackService with a live Player.Listener that keeps mutating the tile; only process death cleans it up. Violates listener-symmetry / 'one owner per player-facing resource'.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: In the buildAsync callback, if the tile is no longer listening (or mediaController already set), release the freshly built controller immediately; also release any existing controller at the top of connectToSession().

p2Appendix.title: MediaExtractor released only inside the use-block happy path - leaks native extractor when openFileDescriptor returns null or setDataSource/getTrackFormat throws
p2Appendix.evidence: extractVideoAudioInfo() creates the extractor before the descriptor: `val extractor = MediaExtractor(); context.contentResolver.openFileDescriptor(uri, "r")?.use { pfd -> extractor.setDataSource(pfd.fileDescriptor); ... extractor.release() }` with only `catch (e: Exception) { Timber.w(e, "MediaExtractor failed for SAF URI, using basic metadata only") }` around it (lines 145-176). `extractor.release()` (line 172) is the last statement of the use-block, so (1) if openFileDescriptor returns null the block never runs and the extractor is never released, and (2) if setDataSource or getTrackFormat throws (corrupt/truncated file, revoked SAF grant - the exact case this catch anticipates), the exception skips release(). The enclosing finally (line 196-198) releases only the retriever. Every failed SAF video/audio probe leaks one native MediaExtractor. The sibling MediaMetadataHelper was already fixed for this exact defect class - its finally comments 'Release native MediaExtractor on every path, incl. throws from setDataSource/getTrackFormat (S0726/S0715 P2)' (MediaMetadataHelper.kt:379-381) - SafUriExtractor never got the fix.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Mirror MediaMetadataHelper: move MediaExtractor creation inside a try with `finally { extractor.release() }`, or create it only after a non-null pfd and wrap the whole use-block body.

p2Appendix.title: extractPdfInfo leaks the ParcelFileDescriptor when the PdfRenderer constructor throws (corrupt or password-protected PDF)
p2Appendix.evidence: `val pfd = context.contentResolver.openFileDescriptor(uri, "r"); if (pfd != null) { val pdfRenderer = android.graphics.pdf.PdfRenderer(pfd); val count = pdfRenderer.pageCount; pdfRenderer.close(); pfd.close(); count } else null` wrapped only in `catch (e: Exception) { Timber.w(...); null }` (lines 211-223). Both closes are on the happy path with no finally: PdfRenderer's constructor throws SecurityException for password-protected PDFs and IOException for corrupt ones without closing the descriptor, so the catch swallows the exception and the open ParcelFileDescriptor is abandoned until its CloseGuard finalizer. File-info on any protected/corrupt SAF PDF leaks an fd per call. Violates protocol Layer 3 'resource closure is enforced using .use { } for all Closeable types' (ThumbnailExtractorHelper.extractPdfThumbnail lines 159-163 shows the correct finally-based pattern in the same codebase).
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Wrap pfd/pdfRenderer in `pfd.use { PdfRenderer(it).use { r -> r.pageCount } }` or a try/finally closing both.

p2Appendix.title: remux() leaks a native MediaExtractor when setDataSource fails on a segment file
p2Appendix.evidence: Per segment: `val extractor = MediaExtractor(); try { extractor.setDataSource(segment.absolutePath) } catch (t: Throwable) { return RemuxResult.MuxFailed(codec = "extractor_failed:${segment.name}") }` (lines 54-59). The release finally (`finally { runCatching { extractor.release() } }`, lines 123-125) belongs to the SECOND try block starting at line 60, so the early return at line 58 exits remux() with the freshly created extractor never released; the outer finally (lines 138-143) releases only the muxer. Trigger: a truncated/corrupt downloaded HLS/DASH segment (the exact failure this catch handles) leaks one native MediaExtractor per remux attempt. Same defect class as the S0726/S0715 P2 fix applied to MediaMetadataHelper.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Fold setDataSource into the second try so the existing `finally { extractor.release() }` covers it, e.g. create the extractor, then one try { setDataSource(...); ... } finally { release() } with the MuxFailed return inside.

p2Appendix.title: M3U playlist import writes N rows as N separate transactions (no withTransaction), unlike the sibling mergeCatalog
p2Appendix.evidence: `suspend fun addAllIgnoringDuplicates(sources: List<StreamSourceEntity>): Int { var inserted = 0; for (source in sources) { if (dao.insertIgnore(source) != -1L) inserted++ }; return inserted }` - called from ImportStreamPlaylistUseCase.kt:52 with every entry of a user-supplied M3U playlist (IPTV lists run to thousands of rows; the same file's S0821 comment documents catalogs exceeding the 999 bind-variable limit). Each insertIgnore is its own implicit transaction (per-row fsync) and each invalidates stream_sources, so active collectors of observeAll/observePinned re-query and re-emit once per inserted row during the import; a process kill mid-loop leaves a partial import with no all-or-nothing boundary. The same class of defect was already fixed for mergeCatalog in this file: lines 74-77 'S0732: N update/insertIgnore writes plus the final catalog prune were not atomic... One transaction makes the catalog sync all-or-nothing (single observe* emission)' - addAllIgnoringDuplicates was left out. Violates Layer 4 'multi-step writes that must be atomic are wrapped in @Transaction'.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Wrap the loop in db.withTransaction { } (the AppDatabase handle is already injected), matching mergeCatalog.

p2Appendix.title: insertAllAsOverrides is non-transactional and its hasOverrides() guard makes a partial apply permanent
p2Appendix.evidence: `suspend fun insertAllAsOverrides(bindings: List<InputBinding>) { bindings.forEach { ... dao.upsert(InputBindingEntity(...)) } }` - a per-row upsert loop with no transaction. Sole caller is AppStartupInitializer.applyDefaultsChromeOsIfEmpty (AppStartupInitializer.kt:119-121): `if (!bindings.hasOverrides()) { bindings.insertAllAsOverrides(defaultsMapLoader.get().loadChromeOsDefaults()) }` where hasOverrides() is `dao.observeAll().first().isNotEmpty()` (line 53). Concrete failure: process death mid-loop (deferred startup task, freely killable) persists only a prefix of the ChromeOS default bindings; on every next launch hasOverrides() returns true, so the remaining defaults are never applied - a silent, permanent half-configured keymap. Each upsert also invalidates input_bindings, re-running the observeResolvedBindings merge once per row. Violates Layer 4 'multi-step writes that must be atomic are wrapped in @Transaction'.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Make it atomic: a DAO @Insert/@Upsert taking List<InputBindingEntity> (single transaction), or wrap the loop in db.withTransaction.

p2Appendix.title: Favorites import inserts row-by-row without a transaction
p2Appendix.evidence: In invoke(), the per-entry loop (lines 74-123) executes `favoritesDao.insert(entity)` (line 104) once per imported favorite with no @Transaction/withTransaction around the batch. Each insert is a separate transaction that invalidates the favorites table, so live collectors (FavoritesRepositoryImpl.getAllFavorites feeding the favorites screen, FavoritesDao.getFileFavorites feeding widget/backup consumers) re-query and re-emit once per imported row, and a process kill mid-import commits an arbitrary prefix of the file with no all-or-nothing boundary - the result summary (imported/skipped counts) is then never shown and the user cannot tell what landed. Contrast: the backup-restore path wraps its favorites writes in `db.withTransaction` (ApplyBackupPayloadUseCase.kt:78). Violates Layer 4 'multi-step writes that must be atomic are wrapped in @Transaction'.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Inject AppDatabase and wrap the import loop in db.withTransaction { } (per-entry try/catch can stay - a failed row does not need to abort the batch), matching ApplyBackupPayloadUseCase.

p2Appendix.title: Three bare lifecycleScope.launch{...collect} sites drive view-bound work (GL video effects, Glide image re-display) with no repeatOnLifecycle - keeps collecting and re-rendering while the Activity is stopped (baselined in unsafe-collect gate, still live)
p2Appendix.evidence: Line 568-574: `activity.lifecycleScope.launch { activity.viewModel.stereoMode.filter { it != StereoMode.AUTO }.collect { mode -> activity.videoPlayerManager.applyStereoEffect(mode) } }`; line 578-589 collects stereoMode and calls `activity.imageLoadingManager.displayImage(path)`; line 593-605 collects `settingsRepository.getSettings().map { it.panelStereoSingleEye }` and also calls displayImage. lifecycleScope only cancels at DESTROY, so with the player Activity STOPPED (recents/another app/multi-window) a settings write (e.g. panelStereoSingleEye toggled from another window or settings sync) triggers a Glide decode + image display into the invisible Activity's views; the DataStore upstream also stays subscribed for the whole background period. These 3 sites are part of the 8 counted by assert-unsafe-collect.ps1 (baseline 8, actual 8); CODE_AUDIT_PROTOCOL Layer 2 requires repeatOnLifecycle/flowWithLifecycle for UI collection. No retained-object leak (scope dies with Activity), hence P2 missing lifecycle-awareness.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Wrap in repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED) or route through the project's collectOnLifecycle helper; the current value re-applies on restart via StateFlow replay.

p2Appendix.title: Warm-up collectors on settings and destinations Flows use bare lifecycleScope.launch{collect} - DataStore and Room upstreams stay actively collected the entire time BrowseActivity sits stopped in the back stack (baselined, still live)
p2Appendix.evidence: Lines 553-558: `lifecycleScope.launch { settingsRepository.getSettings().collect { latestSettings = it } }` and `lifecycleScope.launch { getDestinationsUseCase().collect { latestHasDestinations = it.isNotEmpty() } }` (no repeatOnLifecycle, counted in the unsafe-collect baseline of 8). BrowseActivity commonly remains alive-but-stopped behind PlayerActivity for whole playback sessions; every settings write and every destinations-table change during that time re-runs these collectors and keeps the Room/DataStore subscriptions active in the background. Unlike LyricsManager.kt:42-44 and SlideshowResourceAvailabilityManager.kt:35-37, these two sites carry no justification comment for a lifetime collect. No leak (fields only, scope cancels at destroy) - P2 per taxonomy (missing lifecycle-awareness / over-eager background work).
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Convert to repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED) (values refresh on restart before any menu tap can occur) or document why background freshness is required, as the two justified lifetime-collect sites do.

p2Appendix.title: Entering Picture-in-Picture pauses video: manager-level ON_PAUSE handler lacks the PiP guard the Activity has
p2Appendix.evidence: VideoPlayerManager is a DefaultLifecycleObserver on the Activity lifecycle (VideoPlayerManager.kt:562-564 `lifecycle.addObserver(this)`, PlayerViewerFactory.kt:15 `lifecycle = activity.lifecycle`) and its onPause (VideoPlayerManager.kt:779) delegates unconditionally to onPause() here, lines 52-59: `manager.flushWatchClock(); wasPlayingBeforePause = ..; manager.pause(); manager.stopPositionSaving()`. PlayerActivity.onPause() deliberately skips its own pause work in PiP - PlayerActivity.kt:963-966 `super.onPause(); if (isInPictureInPictureMode) return` - but super.onPause() already dispatched ON_PAUSE to all lifecycle observers, so the player is paused anyway. PictureInPictureManager.onPictureInPictureModeChanged(true) (PictureInPictureManager.kt:101-119) only hides chrome/registers the receiver and never resumes. Runtime path: video playing -> PiP button or auto-enter on home (API 31+) -> activity enters PiP paused state -> ON_PAUSE dispatch pauses ExoPlayer -> PiP window shows a frozen frame until the user taps the remote PLAY action; position auto-save also stops while PiP is 'playing'.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Gate the manager pause on PiP, e.g. route through the host (PlayerCallback) with an isInPictureInPictureMode check, or move the pause to ON_STOP which does not fire while in PiP.

p2Appendix.title: releasePlayer() releases the ExoPlayer while it is still attached to PlayerView - no setVideoSurface(null)/player detach before release (asymmetric with onDestroy)
p2Appendix.evidence: releasePlayer() lines 33-38: `manager.exoPlayer?.let { player -> player.removeListener(manager.playerListener); player.release(); manager.exoPlayer = null }` - there is no `currentPlayerView?.player = null` or clearVideoSurface() before release(), and currentPlayerView keeps referencing the released instance afterwards. The destroy path does it correctly and in the right order: onDestroy() lines 84-92 removes the listener then `manager.currentPlayerView?.player = null` BEFORE `playerToRelease?.release()` (line 105). The project itself documents why surface detach before/at release matters on this codec stack: PlayerActivityLifecycleBridge.kt:60 'Without this CCodec keeps the Surface alive across ATMS window transition (permanent black screen..)'. Runtime path: switching video -> image/PDF (PlayerLifecycleManager.stopVideoPlayback() lines 627-634 -> pause()+releasePlayer()), the periodic recreate (VideoPlaybackPreflightHelper.kt:98-102), and every protocol-swap releasePlayer() all release with the surface still attached. Violates contract item 3.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: In releasePlayer(), detach first: `manager.currentPlayerView?.player = null` (or player.clearVideoSurface()) before removeListener/release, mirroring onDestroy().

p2Appendix.title: Orphan creation path: releaseResources() constructs a brand-new VideoPlayerManager during Activity.onDestroy when none exists (dead catch never fires)
p2Appendix.evidence: Lines 226-230: `try { activity.videoPlayerManager.releasePlayer() } catch (e: UninitializedPropertyAccessException) { // Not initialized, skip }`. But videoPlayerManager is not lateinit - it is a lazily-creating getter, PlayerActivity.kt:132-134: `internal val videoPlayerManager: VideoPlayerManager get() = _videoPlayerManager ?: PlayerViewerFactory(this).createVideoPlayerManager().also { _videoPlayerManager = it }` - so the catch is dead code and the intended skip never happens. Runtime path: any player session that never played video/audio in-app (image, PDF, text - _videoPlayerManager == null) -> PlayerActivity.onDestroy() (line 1028) -> releaseResources() -> the getter builds a full VideoPlayerManager mid-teardown: its init registers a lifecycle observer (VideoPlayerManager.kt:562-564) and launches two settings collectors in managerScope (VideoPlayerManager.kt:373-398), then releasePlayer() immediately early-returns (VideoPlayerLifecycleHelper.kt:21). Cleanup only happens because super.onDestroy() later dispatches ON_DESTROY to the just-added observer. Wasteful construction plus observer registration on every non-video session teardown; contract item 1 (no orphan creation path). PlayerActivity.releasePlayer() (line 935-937) shows the correct `_videoPlayerManager != null` guard.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Use the null-safe backing field: `activity._videoPlayerManager?.releasePlayer()` and delete the dead catch.

p2Appendix.title: Stream error-recovery jobs (up to 5 s / 16 s delayed) act on whatever exoPlayer is current, not the errored instance - yanks the next file's restored position
p2Appendix.evidence: StreamPlaybackHelper.kt:183-187 (BehindLiveWindow branch): 'managerScope.launch { delay(backoffMs); exoPlayer?.seekToDefaultPosition(); exoPlayer?.prepare() }' and :199-203 (transient branch): 'managerScope.launch { delay(backoffMs); if (!isRtsp && exoPlayer?.isCurrentMediaItemLive == true) exoPlayer?.seekToDefaultPosition(); exoPlayer?.prepare() }'. The lambdas read the manager field 'exoPlayer', not the player the listener was attached to; backoff reaches 5 s (behind-live) and 16 s (STREAM_TRANSIENT_BASE_DELAY_MS shl 3, :197/:267-269). managerScope is cancelled only at onDestroy (VideoPlayerLifecycleHelper.kt:125), and releasePlayer() does not cancel these jobs. Runtime path: live stream errors with BEHIND_LIVE_WINDOW -> recovery job scheduled -> within the backoff the user switches to another file -> releasePlayer() + new player created and its saved position restored (VideoPlayerManager.kt:659-669 'exoPlayer?.seekTo(savedPosition)') -> the stale job fires and calls seekToDefaultPosition() on the NEW player, discarding the restored position (VOD jumps to its default start); prepare() is a no-op unless IDLE but the seek is user-visible.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Capture the player instance in the listener closure and guard the delayed block with 'if (exoPlayer !== erroredPlayer) return@launch', or cancel pending recovery jobs in releasePlayer().

p2Appendix.title: Glide targets never cleared on teardown and loads bound to applicationContext - in-flight request retains ImageView/Activity past onDestroy (contract item 9)
p2Appendix.evidence: All three image paths load via the application-scoped RequestManager: showImage lines 343-345 `Glide.with(activity.applicationContext).load(mediaFile.path.toUri()).into(safeViews.photoView)`, showGif lines 366-369 (`.asGif()` same pattern), reloadImage lines 355-360. An application-scoped RequestManager is not paused or cleared when the host Activity is destroyed, so an in-flight decode keeps its ViewTarget -> photoView -> Activity context reachable until the load completes, and the completed drawable is set on a dead view. release() (lines 293-334, the manager's teardown edge called from StandalonePlayerActivity.onDestroy) clears players, viewers, and focus but contains no `Glide.with(...).clear(safeViews.photoView)` - confirmed by reading the whole file: no clear() call exists anywhere in the class. Violates CODE_AUDIT_PROTOCOL Layer 3 Glide ownership: 'clear(target) on detach; do not bind Glide.with(activity) to a long-lived target'. Runtime path: open a large IMAGE/GIF via the standalone host, press back while the decode is still running -> Activity destroyed, request keeps running and retains the view hierarchy until decode finishes (transient retention, not a proven persistent leak -> P2). Note the loads also skip `override(w,h)` (decode at full source resolution into a fullscreen target).
p2Appendix.fix_hint: In release() add `Glide.with(activity.applicationContext).clear(safeViews.photoView)` (clear works on any RequestManager), or switch loads to `Glide.with(activity)` so the request auto-cancels with the host lifecycle.

p2Appendix.title: Video ExoPlayer released only in onDestroy - prepared player and codecs held for unbounded time while the activity is stopped in background (contract item 2)
p2Appendix.evidence: The only release edge is onDestroy() line 445-457 (`viewManager.release()` line 455). There is no onStop override anywhere in the activity (full read: only onCreate/onPause/onDestroy/onUserLeaveHint/onConfigurationChanged/onPictureInPictureModeChanged/onResumeWithViews exist) and StandalonePlayerLifecycleManager has no onStop hook (StandalonePlayerLifecycleManager.kt:18-35). onPause only flips the flag: StandaloneViewManager.onPause lines 286-291 `exoPlayer?.playWhenReady = false ...` - the player stays prepared with its MediaItem, surface and decoders attached. CODE_AUDIT_PROTOCOL Layer 3 requires 'release on onStop for API 24+ multi-window, re-create on onStart' or a deliberate documented alternative; the only documented deviation is the PiP onPause skip (lines 437-443: 'Skip pausing playback when entering PiP...'), which explains onPause but not holding the player past onStop - releasing in onStop would remain PiP-compatible (onStop does not fire while the PiP window is showing). Runtime path: open a video in the standalone host, press Home (no PiP, or PiP disabled) -> activity stopped, task parked in recents -> the ExoPlayer instance plus hardware codecs stay allocated indefinitely until the system kills the process or the user returns/swipes. Held-not-leaked (released at destroy, and manifest configChanges line 540 prevents rotation teardown), so P2 missing lifecycle-awareness rather than P1.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Release the player in onStop and rebuild in onStart (guarding the PiP case), or document the keep-alive-in-background decision at the release site as the contract's deliberate alternative.

p2Appendix.title: Player released on onDestroy instead of the API24+ onStop edge, with no documenting comment for the deviation - codecs held while the host sits stopped in background
p2Appendix.evidence: Teardown edges: onPause() lines 1006-1011 only sets playWhenReady=false via viewManager.onPause() ('val isInPip = ...; if (!isInPip) viewManager.onPause()'), and the player is released only in onDestroy() lines 1013-1024 ('viewManager.release()' line 1022). There is no onStop/onStart pair, so on API 24+ (minSdk 26) a HOME-press or multi-window focus loss leaves the prepared ExoPlayer with its codec resources held for the entire stopped-in-background lifetime until the framework finally destroys the activity. Contract item 2 requires release in onStop / re-create in onStart 'or a deliberate documented alternative': the only nearby comment (line 1007, 'S0393 U1: keep playback running when the activity pauses to enter PiP') documents the PiP pause exception, not the choice of the onDestroy release edge. Mirrors the unified host exactly (StandalonePlayerActivity.onPause lines 437-443 / onDestroy line 455 'viewManager.release()'), so this is family-consistent rather than divergence, and the player IS released on real teardown - hence P2 (missing lifecycle-awareness without a proven leak), not P1.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Either release in onStop and rebuild/restore position in onStart (guard with isInPictureInPictureMode, since onStop does not fire while pipped), or add an explicit comment at onDestroy documenting the deliberate alternative (PiP keep-alive + configChanges no-recreate rationale).

p2Appendix.title: SAF rename restarts audio playback from position 0 (and leaks the just-swapped controller): path change from onRenameComplete re-triggers viewManager.show() because lastShownPath is not updated on rename
p2Appendix.evidence: Rename flow (StandaloneFileOperationsHandler.kt lines 520-527) calls `onRenameComplete(newUri, newName)` then `updateAudioMediaItem(newUri)`. The VM (StandalonePlayerViewModel.onRenameComplete, lines 312-320) does `state.copy(mediaFile = state.mediaFile?.copy(name=newName, path=newUri.toString(), contentUri=newUri.toString()))` - state.mediaFile.path changes. updateAudioMediaItem performs the intended seamless swap (`player.replaceMediaItem(0, ...)`; `player.seekTo(currentPosition)`, StandaloneViewManager.kt lines 517-523, with the activity comment line 183 'A SAF rename must keep the background-service playback uninterrupted'). But the state collector then resumes on main with the new path and hits lines 519-522: `if (file.path != lastShownPath) { viewManager.show(file, MediaType.AUDIO); lastShownPath = file.path ... }` - lastShownPath still holds the pre-rename path, so show() -> playAudio() runs: a NEW AudioServiceController is created (orphaning the one that just did the seamless replaceMediaItem) and its onConnected does `player.setMediaItem(mediaItem); player.prepare(); player.play()` (AudioServiceController.kt lines 148-152), resetting the service player to position 0. Concrete trigger: rename the currently playing audio file via btnRenameCmd when SAF returns a new URI (`if (newUri != uri)`) - playback audibly restarts from the beginning, defeating the documented uninterrupted-rename contract.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Update lastShownPath inside the onRenameComplete wiring (it already knows newUri), or compare a rename-stable identity instead of raw path in the collector.

p2Appendix.title: onDestroy final-position save is cancelled by serviceScope.cancel() on the next statement - the destroy-edge save is dead in practice
p2Appendix.evidence: AudioPlaybackService.onDestroy lines 405-414: `if (path != null && finalDur > 0 && finalPos >= 0) { serviceScope.launch(Dispatchers.IO) { try { playbackPositionRepository.savePosition(path, finalPos, finalDur) } catch (e: Exception) { Timber.e(e, "AudioPlaybackService: onDestroy save position failed") } } }` followed immediately by `serviceScope.cancel()` (line 414). The launched coroutine is a child of serviceScope (`CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Main)`, line 91); cancel() on the very next statement cancels it before the IO dispatcher runs it, or at its first suspension point - savePosition is suspend end-to-end (PlaybackPositionRepository.kt:14 `suspend fun savePosition(..)` -> Room suspend DAO PlaybackPositionDao.kt:15 `suspend fun savePosition(position: PlaybackPositionEntity)`), so the Room write aborts. The `catch (e: Exception)` at line 409 additionally swallows the CancellationException and logs it as a save failure. Runtime path: network-audio (currentOriginalPath non-empty) playing -> user stops the service mid-track (auto-stop, fatal error stopSelf, MainActivity exit stopService, task-removed stop) -> onDestroy runs -> the code that comments 'Capture position before player is released' (lines 399-403) computes finalPos/finalDur but the persistence coroutine is cancelled -> resume position falls back to the last periodic tick, up to POSITION_SAVE_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000L (line 117) stale. Cleanup-path work defeated by its own teardown ordering (protocol: 'failure paths clean up resources too'); bounded position loss -> P2.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Launch the final save with NonCancellable (`serviceScope.launch(Dispatchers.IO + NonCancellable) { .. }`) or into an injected application-scoped CoroutineScope, and only then cancel serviceScope; rethrow CancellationException in the catch.

p2Appendix.title: Multi-window: first-destroyed PlayerActivity releases the shared singleton player out from under the surviving window and permanently unhooks its UI listeners (contract item 1: host ownership not exclusive)
p2Appendix.evidence: `@Singleton` (line 32) means ALL PlayerActivity instances share one manager + one player, and duplicate live windows are by design: PlayerActivity.tearOffPlayer() (PlayerActivity.kt:822-835, comment "S0184: open a duplicate Player in a new window slot while keeping the source player alive") launches with FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK|FLAG_ACTIVITY_MULTIPLE_TASK (also BrowseEventHandler.kt:287-288); the manifest declares no launchMode (AndroidManifest.xml:212). Runtime path with windows A (slideshow + music playing) and B: (a) B's own state collector (PlayerObserverManager.kt:44-48) calls updateState(B.state); with B not music-eligible the else-branch (lines 202-215) runs `loadPlaylistJob?.cancel()` and `musicPlayer?.clearMediaItems()` (209) - killing A's playing music deterministically; (b) closing B runs PlayerLifecycleManager.kt:186-188 `backgroundMusicManager.release()` -> player released and `onTrackChangedListener = null; onMusicErrorListener = null` (lines 551-552) while A still lives; A's `areAudioBackgroundManagersConfigured` flag is already true so ensureAudioBackgroundManagersConfigured() early-returns (PlayerManagerInitializer.kt:171-173) and never re-wires the listeners -> A's track-name display and error toasts are dead for the rest of its life (music itself lazily re-creates a player via line 231 on A's next eligible state). Duplicate/orphan creation was verified absent (all creation funnels through the null-guarded main-thread initializeInternal, line 96; post-release recovery coroutines are inert because release() empties availableAudioFiles at 546 so skip early-returns at 383), so the defect is host-ownership, not instance duplication.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Refcount configured hosts and release only when the last one is destroyed, or scope the manager to the activity (remove @Singleton) since all state is per-session anyway; at minimum re-wire listeners on window resume.

p2Appendix.title: No audio-focus handling: player built without setAudioAttributes(attrs, handleAudioFocus=true), unlike every other player host in the app (contract item 5, acquisition half)
p2Appendix.evidence: Line 97: `musicPlayer = ExoPlayer.Builder(context).build().apply { volume = 0.5f; prepare(); addListener(...) }` - no AudioAttributes and no focus handling. Every other ExoPlayer host sets it: PlayerSetupHelper.kt:48 `.setAudioAttributes(audioAttributes, true) // handleAudioFocus=true`, AudioPlaybackService.kt:197, LocalPlaybackHelper.kt:104, SmbPlaybackHelper.kt:120, SftpPlaybackHelper.kt:115, FtpPlaybackHelper.kt:106, CloudPlaybackHelper.kt:71, StreamPlaybackHelper.kt:72, AudioEmptyStateController.kt:257. Runtime path: slideshow background music starts while another app is playing audio -> both play mixed (this app never requests focus, so the other app is not paused/ducked), and on transient focus events (call, navigation prompt) the music keeps playing because nothing pauses it. Consequently the release contract's "abandon audio focus on release" is vacuous - focus was never acquired. The playWhenReady half of item 5 IS satisfied: release() destroys the instance and resets isPlaying (line 541); re-init creates a fresh player with playWhenReady=false.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Build with AudioAttributes(USAGE_MEDIA/CONTENT_TYPE_MUSIC) and handleAudioFocus=true, matching PlayerSetupHelper.kt:48.

p2Appendix.title: stop() leaves playWhenReady=true and the playlist loaded on the service player, defeating AudioPlaybackService.onTaskRemoved's no-active-playback stopSelf heuristic
p2Appendix.evidence: Service branch of stopPlaybackKeepingController(): `player?.stop()` (line 183) - Media3 Player.stop() transitions to STATE_IDLE but does not reset playWhenReady and does not clear media items. AudioPlaybackService.onTaskRemoved (AudioPlaybackService.kt:381-391) decides whether to stop: `if (currentPlayer == null || !currentPlayer.playWhenReady || currentPlayer.mediaItemCount == 0 || currentPlayer.playbackState == Player.STATE_ENDED) { ... stopSelf() } // If still playing, let the service continue`. After the user stops an inline ON-mode stream, the service player is IDLE with playWhenReady still true and mediaItemCount 1, so every disjunct is false and onTaskRemoved skips stopSelf for a service that is NOT playing anything. The service's own auto-stop timer is armed only on STATE_ENDED (AudioPlaybackService.kt:206-219); the STATE_IDLE branch (lines 235-238) only stops position saving. Concrete path: play inline radio with background playback ON -> tap the mini-control stop -> swipe the app away from recents -> the idle service (with its ExoPlayer and MediaSession) is deliberately left running by the misfired heuristic instead of stopping. Violates contract item 5 ('playWhenReady reset') and weakens item 7 (onTaskRemoved early-exit path); lifetime is ultimately bounded by OS background-service limits, hence P2 not P1.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: In the service branch of stopPlaybackKeepingController(), also reset the flag before/after stop: `player?.playWhenReady = false` (or `player?.clearMediaItems()`), so onTaskRemoved and any 'is playback active' heuristics see a truly inactive player; alternatively arm the service auto-stop on STATE_IDLE too.

p2Appendix.title: cancelAll() cannot stop queued captures: drainOne polls the url before suspending on the semaphore, so parked drainOnes launch full ExoPlayer captures after onStop / leaving GRID
p2Appendix.evidence: drainOne (lines 102-104): `val url = queue.poll() ?: return` executes BEFORE `semaphore.withPermit {` - the url leaves the queue before the coroutine parks waiting for a permit. With the host's lifecycleScope (Dispatchers.Main.immediate, StreamsActivity:110) every `request()` runs its `scope.launch { drainOne() }` (line 89) synchronously to the first suspension, so with N visible tiles all N urls are polled within milliseconds while only 2 captures hold permits (MAX_CONCURRENT_CAPTURES=2). cancelAll (lines 93-100) then does `queue.clear()` (already empty - no-op), `pending.clear()`, and cancels only `inFlight` - which contains ONLY the launched capture jobs (added at line 112); the N-2 parked drainOne coroutines are tracked nowhere. After cancelAll they acquire freed permits and run `scope.launch { capture(url) }` (line 105) on the still-alive lifecycleScope: each creates an ExoPlayer, opens the network and decodes up to CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS=12 s, two at a time. This directly defeats the documented contract - line 92 'Clear the queue and cancel in-flight captures (leaving GRID / on stop)' and StreamsActivity:736 'S0675: never run frame captures while backgrounded' (onStop:739 calls cancelAll) and StreamGridModeManager:82 (applyMode(LIST) calls cancelAll). Concrete path: GRID with 10 visible video tiles, pull-to-refresh enqueues 10, user presses Home -> onStop -> cancelAll kills 2; the remaining 8 captures run serially in background for up to ~48 s (network + decoder + onOutcome DB writes). Every player is still released in capture's finally, so this is background work after teardown, not a resource leak (P2 per taxonomy: missing lifecycle-awareness without a proven leak).
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Poll the url inside withPermit after acquiring, and re-check a generation/cancelled marker after acquire; or track drainOne jobs in inFlight too; or launch all work under a child SupervisorJob that cancelAll cancels and recreates.

p2Appendix.title: Inline audio plays without ever requesting audio focus, so release has nothing to abandon and playback ignores focus loss (contract item 5)
p2Appendix.evidence: Playback starts at line 181 'newPlayer.start()' and stops at lines 86-94 ('fun inlineStop() { player?.let { try { it.stop() } .. it.release() } .. }') with zero AudioManager/AudioFocusRequest usage anywhere in the class; grep over ui/browse shows audio-focus handling exists only in BrowseMicRecordingManager.kt (requestAudioFocus line 74/83, abandonAudioFocus lines 232-244) - nothing acquires focus on behalf of inline playback. Runtime path: user starts inline audio while another app plays music -> both streams mix (no AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN request), and when another app later takes focus (navigation prompt, incoming media app) inline audio keeps playing because no OnAudioFocusChangeListener exists. The release-side of item 5 is vacuous only because acquisition is missing entirely.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Request AudioFocusRequest(AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN) with an OnAudioFocusChangeListener (pause on transient loss, stop on loss) before start(), and abandonAudioFocusRequest in inlineStop(); mirror the existing BrowseMicRecordingManager pattern.

p2Appendix.title: playerWarmupJob / audioMetadataEnrichmentJob / lastWarmupSignature written on IO dispatcher but cancelled/read from main thread without synchronization - cancel edge can miss the live job
p2Appendix.evidence: Lines 60-62: 'private var playerWarmupJob: Job? = null .. private var audioMetadataEnrichmentJob: Job? = null' - plain vars. Writers run on the IO dispatcher: schedulePlayerWarmupIfEligible (lines 288-292: 'lastWarmupSignature = sig; playerWarmupJob?.cancel(); playerWarmupJob = scope.launch {..}') is invoked from coroutines launched with 'scope.launch(ioDispatcher + exceptionHandler)' in BrowseResourceLoadManager (launch sites lines 105 and 312; call sites lines 216, 265, 467), and enrichAudioMetadataInBackground (lines 210-211: 'audioMetadataEnrichmentJob?.cancel(); audioMetadataEnrichmentJob = scope.launch(ioDispatcher + exceptionHandler)') is called from the same IO coroutine via onFilesLoadedSaveAndEnrich (BrowseViewModel.kt:471). Readers run on main: cancelPlayerWarmup() (lines 309-311) <- BrowseViewModel.cancelScan:736 <- BrowseActivity.onStop:642, and cancelAll() (lines 314-317) <- BrowseViewModel.onCleared:663. With no @Volatile/Mutex the main thread can read a stale null/old Job and skip cancelling the just-assigned one (e.g. onStop's 'cancelScan(forceCancel = true)' misses a warmup scheduled concurrently by the finishing load). P2 not P1 because impact is bounded: all jobs are viewModelScope children (killed at clear anyway) and the warmup player self-releases in the same statement (line 296 'ExoPlayer.Builder(context).build().release()') - no resource can remain held.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Confine job-field mutation to the main dispatcher (make schedulePlayerWarmupIfEligible hop via withContext(Dispatchers.Main) for the assignment) or mark the fields @Volatile and do cancel-and-assign under a small Mutex.

p2Appendix.title: inline_audio disk cache has no size bound or eviction: every played/prefetched SMB track is stored in full, forever, until a manual whole-cache wipe or OS storage pressure
p2Appendix.evidence: Lines 241-245: 'val cacheDir = java.io.File(context.cacheDir, "inline_audio"); cacheDir.mkdirs(); return java.io.File(cacheDir, "${file.path.hashCode()}_${file.name}")' - and downloadSmbAudioToCache writes the entire remote file (line 292 'java.io.FileOutputStream(cacheFile).use { output -> smbClient.get().downloadFile(..) }'); prefetchNextInlineAudio (lines 202-221) additionally downloads the next track automatically after every start. Grep for 'inline_audio' across app_v2/src/main finds only this method - no size check, LRU trim, or age-based cleanup exists on the write path or anywhere else; the only deletions are the per-file failure cleanup (line 309 'cacheFile.delete()') and the user-triggered Settings 'Clear cache' which wipes the whole cacheDir (GeneralSettingsCacheHelper.kt:127-128 'val cacheDir = fragment.requireContext().cacheDir; deleteRecursive(cacheDir)'). Runtime path: listening through a large SMB music share caches every track at full size (play + prefetch), consuming storage equal to the share's audio volume until the user manually clears cache or the OS trims app cache under low-storage pressure. P2 rather than P1 because cacheDir is OS-evictable and a manual wipe exists, so growth is not strictly unbounded on-device.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Add a bound on the write path: after a successful download, trim inline_audio to a max size (e.g. delete oldest-mtime files beyond N MB), or reuse UnifiedFileCache which already has stats/clearAll infrastructure.

p2Appendix.title: Enable-all sequence stalls permanently after recreation/process death: stage-completion callback is instance-bound and restored inProgress=true has no resume path
p2Appendix.evidence: runGrantAll(onComplete) stores the enable-all continuation only in the in-memory field `private var grantAllOnComplete: (() -> Unit)? = null` (line 75, set at 169); onSaveInstanceState (lines 140-143) persists grantAllInProgress + shownSpecialInRun but not the stage linkage, and attach() (line 78) never re-arms it. The machinery is explicitly designed to survive recreation (stable registry keys, WelcomePermissionsManager.kt:319-323; state restore, WelcomeEnableAllManager.kt:89-93), and WelcomeActivity is recreatable mid-run despite configChanges=orientation|screenSize|keyboardHidden (AndroidManifest.xml:243 lacks uiMode/smallestScreenSize/screenLayout; process death while the user is on a special-permission system screen is the common case). After recreation the pending special-settings ActivityResult IS delivered to the new instance's callback (stable key KEY_SPECIAL_SETTINGS) and the walk correctly continues on restored state, but at its end `grantAllOnComplete?.invoke()` (line 219) is null on the new instance - so WelcomeEnableAllManager.beginDefaultPlayerStage/finishSequence/onFinished (completeWelcomeFlow) never run, and the new enable-all manager's restored inProgress=true blocks any re-tap forever (`if (inProgress) return`, WelcomeEnableAllManager.kt:98) and is re-saved on every later recreation. Secondary mechanism in the pre-walk window: the appScope coroutine in start() (WelcomeEnableAllManager.kt:105-115) captures the pre-recreation `pm` and manager instances; resumed after a recreation it drives pm.runGrantAll against the DESTROYED Activity (WelcomePermissionsManager.activity is never cleared - no detach exists) and its dead ActivityResultRegistry launchers, and the final finishSequence invokes completeWelcomeFlow/finish() on the destroyed instance while the visible instance never advances. Failure scenario: tap 'Enable all' -> OS opens the MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE settings screen -> process is killed in background (or auto dark-mode flips uiMode) -> user returns: permissions finish, but onboarding never completes and the Enable-all button stays dead for the session. No crash/leak proof, so P2 (missing lifecycle-awareness / broken cross-recreation state machine).
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Persist the stage in the Bundle and rebuild the linkage on restore: in WelcomeEnableAllManager.attach(), when restored inProgress==true, re-arm permissionsManager.grantAllOnComplete (and resume the correct stage); resolve activity/pm at resume time instead of capturing them in the appScope closure; clear WelcomePermissionsManager.activity/binding on host destroy.

p2Appendix.title: shutdownRenderThreadSync abandons a still-alive render thread that strongly references the Activity and the live native EGL/OpenXR session on join timeout
p2Appendix.evidence: Lines 1120-1128: `thread.requestExit(); thread.join(timeoutMs); if (thread.isAlive) { Timber.w("...render thread did not exit within ${timeoutMs}ms") }; renderThread = null; sessionReady = false`. DiagnosticXrRenderThread holds `private val activity: Activity` (DiagnosticXrRenderThread.kt line 29) plus three activity method references (onSessionReady/onExitDelivered/onStartFailed, lines 46-48) and blocks inside `runtime.runFrameLoop()` (line 107). If the native frame loop does not observe the exit flag within PAUSE_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS=2000 (onPause) / SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS=3000 (onDestroy), the only reference is nulled while the thread keeps running: the destroyed Activity stays reachable from a live thread and the EGL/OpenXR session survives host teardown, with no retry/re-join/watchdog left to reclaim either. The ExoPlayer itself is not affected (released at lines 1106/1112 before the join), so this is a residual-resource path, not a player leak; per taxonomy this is missing lifecycle-awareness without a proven leak -> P2.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: After a timed-out join, keep a weak handle and escalate (second join on onDestroy, or a watchdog that logs/reports if the thread is still alive N seconds later); ensure the thread's callbacks null out or no-op once abandoned so a late finally-block cannot call into a destroyed Activity.

p2Appendix.title: Contract item 2: no onStop handling - video/audio playback keeps running while the host activity is stopped; onCleared is the only teardown edge
p2Appendix.evidence: The sole teardown is `override fun onCleared() { .. exoPlayer.removeListener(playerListener); exoPlayer.release() }` (VideoPlayerViewModel.kt:333-343; same in AudioPlayerViewModel.kt:301-309). Grep over wear/src/main for `onStop|onPause|Ambient|LifecycleEventObserver|LocalLifecycleOwner|repeatOnLifecycle` returns no matches; MainActivity has only `onCreate` (MainActivity.kt:41). Runtime path: user plays a video, presses home/palm-over (activity ON_STOP, composition retained, VM alive) - the per-VM ExoPlayer keeps decoding video+audio invisibly on the watch until the OS kills the process; there is no foreground service or MediaSession legitimizing background playback. The S0725 comments (VideoPlayerViewModel.kt:339-341, WearAppModule.kt:58-63) document per-VM ownership vs the old singleton but do not document a deliberate keep-playing-while-stopped decision, so the protocol's 'release in onStop / recreate in onStart, or a deliberate documented alternative' is not met for the ON_STOP edge. No proven leak (release still happens at VM clear) - P2 missing lifecycle-awareness.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Observe host lifecycle (e.g. LifecycleEventObserver or collectAsStateWithLifecycle-driven callback) and at least exoPlayer.pause() on ON_STOP for both VMs; or document background audio as intended and back it with a MediaSession + foreground service.

p2Appendix.title: Contract item 5: player never requests audio focus - builder omits setAudioAttributes(attrs, handleAudioFocus=true)
p2Appendix.evidence: `return androidx.media3.exoplayer.ExoPlayer.Builder(context).setHandleAudioBecomingNoisy(true).build()` (WearAppModule.kt:68-70). Media3 1.2.1 ExoPlayer.Builder defaults to AudioAttributes.DEFAULT with handleAudioFocus=false, so neither the audio nor the video player ever requests audio focus. Runtime path: start music in AudioPlayerScreen while another watch app (or paired-headphones stream) is playing - both audio streams mix; conversely other apps starting playback do not pause/duck this player. The release-side of item 5 is vacuous (nothing to abandon; release() is called in both VMs), but 'focus handling' per the unit contract is absent entirely.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Build with .setAudioAttributes(AudioAttributes.Builder().setUsage(C.USAGE_MEDIA).setContentType(C.AUDIO_CONTENT_TYPE_MUSIC/MOVIE).build(), /* handleAudioFocus= */ true); release() then abandons focus automatically.

p2Appendix.title: Contract item 5 (playWhenReady reset): audio STATE_ENDED seeks to 0 without pausing - track restarts and loops indefinitely
p2Appendix.evidence: `Player.STATE_ENDED -> { _uiState.update { it.copy(isPlaying = false, currentPositionMs = 0) }; exoPlayer.seekTo(0); publishPlaybackState() }` (AudioPlayerViewModel.kt:92-96). playWhenReady is set true at load (lines 150, 198) and never reset before the seek; seeking out of STATE_ENDED with playWhenReady=true resumes playback (standard ExoPlayer replay semantics), so every track end restarts the track - an unintended infinite repeat that also burns watch battery and publishes isPlaying=false to the phone while audio is actually playing again. The video VM explicitly avoids this: `exoPlayer.pause(); exoPlayer.seekTo(0)` with comment 'Seek to start for replay, but pause' (VideoPlayerViewModel.kt:93-95).
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Mirror the video handler: call exoPlayer.pause() before exoPlayer.seekTo(0) in the STATE_ENDED branch.

p2Appendix.title: SMB playback temp files are re-downloaded every open and never deleted - cache dirs grow without app-side bound on watch storage
p2Appendix.evidence: `val cacheDir = File(context.cacheDir, "smb_video"); cacheDir.mkdirs(); .. val tempFile = File(cacheDir, tempFileName) .. FileOutputStream(tempFile).use { output -> input.copyTo(output) }` (VideoPlayerViewModel.kt:207-221); identical pattern in AudioPlayerViewModel.kt:174-188 (`smb_audio`). Grep for `cacheDir|smb_video|smb_audio` across wear/src/main shows only these writers - no delete/trim anywhere, and no exists-check, so each playback of an SMB file re-downloads the full media over SMB and overwrites the temp file, while distinct files accumulate forever. Runtime path: browse an SMB source and play N different videos - N full video files pile up in cacheDir on a small-storage watch until OS storage-pressure cache trimming (the only backstop, hence P2 rather than the taxonomy's P1 for unbounded in-memory caches). Cancelled mid-download coroutines also leave partial files behind. Same out-of-unit pattern exists in ImageViewerViewModel.kt:105-110 (`smb_images`) - /spec-draft candidate for the caller.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Reuse an existing complete temp file (skip download), delete the temp file in onCleared, and/or LRU-trim the smb_* cache dirs to a fixed byte budget; apply the same fix to ImageViewerViewModel.

p2Appendix.title: Unguarded suspend settings write between successful VR dispatch and finishAndRemoveTask() - failure path skips 2D-host teardown and crashes via uncaught exception
p2Appendix.evidence: PlayerVrLaunchManager.kt:122-126: `when (val result = startVrPlaybackUseCase(request, returnTarget)) { StartVrPlaybackUseCase.DispatchResult.Started -> { markPromptDismissed(); activity.finishAndRemoveTask() } ... }`. At this point the VR host activity has ALREADY been started (StartVrPlaybackUseCaseImpl.kt:79 `appContext.startActivity(intent)` succeeded before returning Started). `markPromptDismissed()` (lines 362-366) calls `settingsRepository.updateSettings(settings.copy(vrPlayerEntryPromptDismissed = true))`, which executes an unprotected `dataStore.edit { .. }` (SettingsRepositoryImpl.kt:556 - no try/catch anywhere in that chain; only the read at line 534 is wrapped in runCatching). The enclosing coroutine is `launchJob = activity.lifecycleScope.launch { .. }` (line 107) whose only try/catch (lines 113-119) covers `buildStartRequest` exclusively; lifecycleScope has no CoroutineExceptionHandler. Runtime path (vr flavor, first badge/overflow VR launch while vrPlayerEntryPromptDismissed==false): DataStore write fails (IOException is DataStore's documented write-failure mode) -> exception propagates out of markPromptDismissed -> uncaught in lifecycleScope -> process crash while the immersive host is starting, and `activity.finishAndRemoveTask()` on line 125 never executes, so the hand-off never tears down the 2D player host. Violates contract item 7 (failure/early-exit paths must release/tear down too). P2, not P1/P0: the trigger is an environmental I/O failure; static review confirms the unprotected structure, not runtime frequency.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Reorder to `activity.finishAndRemoveTask()` before the settings write, or wrap markPromptDismissed() in runCatching (a lost prompt-dismissed flag is harmless; a skipped teardown/crash is not).

p2Appendix.title: 500 ms position poll keeps running in background while sheet host is stopped - keyed to isPlaying only, never to view visibility
p2Appendix.evidence: startPositionPoll() runs in viewModelScope with no lifecycle tie: 'positionPollJob = viewModelScope.launch { while (isActive) { val c = mediaController; if (c != null && c.isConnected) { _state.value = _state.value.copy(positionMs = c.currentPosition.coerceAtLeast(0L), durationMs = c.duration.coerceAtLeast(0L)) }; delay(POSITION_POLL_INTERVAL_MS) } }' (lines 170-184). It is stopped only by onIsPlayingChanged(false) (line 71) or disconnect() (line 141), and disconnect() is called only from NowPlayingBottomSheetFragment.onDestroyView (line 86). Concrete runtime path: audio playing via AudioPlaybackService -> user opens the Now Playing sheet -> presses Home. Background playback is the feature, so isPlaying stays true and onIsPlayingChanged(false) never fires; onDestroyView does not fire because the dialog is not dismissed. Meanwhile the only consumer, collectOnLifecycle(viewModel.state) (fragment line 146), uses viewLifecycleOwner.repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) (LifecycleExtensions.kt lines 22-24), which suspends collection at onStop. Result: the coroutine wakes every 500 ms, reads controller position, allocates a NowPlayingState copy and emits to a collector-less StateFlow indefinitely (hours-long listening sessions) until the sheet is dismissed or the process dies. Violates the protocol Layer 2 rule that upstream work stops when nothing observes (missing lifecycle-awareness without a proven leak = P2). Not P1: no leak (all refs are VM-scoped and released at onDestroyView), no I/O (MediaController.getCurrentPosition is a local estimate, no binder call), bounded allocation rate.
p2Appendix.fix_hint: Pause the poll when the host view drops below STARTED: have the fragment call viewModel-side pausePoll()/resumePoll() from onStop()/onStart(), or drive the poll from a flow collected via repeatOnLifecycle so cancellation is automatic (e.g. expose position as a flow { while(true) { emit(..); delay(500) } } that the fragment collects with collectOnLifecycle, keeping the VM free of a self-running timer).
